stories.headline: Trump says US 'doesn't need' an Iran deal as Hormuz tanker blasts and Houthi strikes lift oil 3%

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 12 Trump posted on Truth Social that the US no longer needs a deal with Iran: 'We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!'
key_facts.excerpt: "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Trump said in a Truth Social post.

key_facts.fact: Brent settled up $3.06 (3.3%) at $95.82 a barrel and WTI up $2.21 (2.6%) at $88.74 on Nov. 12, though both were still down about 2.5% for the week.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures settled at $95.82 a barrel, up $3.06 or 3.3%. US West Texas Intermediate crude closed at $88.74 a barrel, up $2.21 or 2.6%. For the week, both benchmarks were still down about 2.5%.

key_facts.fact: Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings; Reuters could not independently verify the claims.
key_facts.excerpt: On Thursday, Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings. Reuters could not immediately verify the Iranian accounts.

key_facts.fact: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they attacked a pumping station on the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, an oil facility in Yanbu and an Aramco building in Riyadh.
key_facts.excerpt: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they had attacked a pumping station on the Saudi East-West oil pipeline; an oil facility in the Saudi Red Sea city of Yanbu; and an Aramco building in the capital Riyadh.

key_facts.fact: Trump separately said he would 'not hesitate' to launch new strikes on Iran if Tehran threatens US allies or ships in Hormuz, adding 'We control the Gulf in terms of the Hormuz Strait.'
key_facts.excerpt: "No, no hesitation," Trump told Salem News Channel... "We control the Gulf in terms of the Hormuz Strait. We totally control it," Trump said.

key_facts.fact: The post puts in question an Iranian proposal Qatar's prime minister reportedly brought to the White House: reopen Hormuz and stop tanker attacks in exchange for lifting the US port blockade and unfreezing $8B held in Qatar (unconfirmed by either government).
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran would open Hormuz again and stop attacking tankers. Washington, for its part, would lift the blockade on Iran's ports and unfreeze $8 billion of Iranian money sitting in Qatar. The two governments have not confirmed any of this.

key_facts.fact: Before the US-Israeli war with Iran, the Strait of Hormuz carried nearly one-fifth of the world's crude oil; the war is about eight months old.
key_facts.excerpt: The Strait of Hormuz carried nearly one-fifth of the world's crude oil before the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.headline: Putin agrees to let Europe join next Ukraine talks round; envoys brief Zelensky in Dublin

key_facts.fact: After meeting Putin in the Kremlin on Nov. 12, US envoy Steve Witkoff said Europeans will join the next round of Ukraine peace talks, a step Reuters called a breakthrough.
key_facts.excerpt: "The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment because they are our partners and it's important to us that they take part," Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin in the Kremlin.

key_facts.fact: Putin warned that the European idea of sending Western troops into Ukraine after a peace deal would trigger a resumption of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: He then warned that the European idea of sending Western troops into Ukraine once a peace deal was concluded would trigger a resumption of the war because Russia would see that as a threat to its own security.

key_facts.fact: Putin proposed a joint Russian-Ukrainian humanitarian mission to Kostiantynivka; the Kremlin said the US side supported it and that Putin would continue Ukraine discussions with Trump at the APEC summit in China.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said Putin would continue discussions on Ukraine with U.S. President Donald Trump at an APEC summit in China later this month... the American side had supported Putin's proposal for a joint humanitarian mission

key_facts.fact: Witkoff and Kushner then met Zelensky the evening of Nov. 12 at Casement Aerodrome near Dublin; Zelensky said Europe will have a negotiating team 'at the table' next time and the coming prisoner swap will be the biggest of the war.
key_facts.excerpt: "Next time, next meeting, Europe...will be in the negotiating team," he said... "It will be the biggest, Steve and Jared told me, the biggest exchange of war prisoners yet," Zelensky said.

key_facts.fact: Kushner said Putin agreed to allow Europe to participate in negotiations: 'he's willing to give it a try.'
key_facts.excerpt: The envoy confirmed that Putin agreed to allow Europe to participate in negotiations regarding ending the war in Ukraine. "(H)e's willing to give it a try," Kushner said.

key_facts.fact: Territory remains unresolved: Russia holds about one fifth of Ukraine and Kyiv refuses to give up the rest of the Donbas.
key_facts.excerpt: Serious unresolved issues remain however, including differences over territory - with Russia holding about one fifth of Ukraine and Kyiv refusing to give up the rest of the Donbas region in its east.

stories.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield climbs back above 5.1% on oil jump and Fed hike bets

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 0.114 percentage point to 5.102% on Nov. 12 (3 p.m. ET), its fourth straight daily rise and highest since Oct. 21.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year yield rose 0.114 percentage point to 5.102% today... Yield is up for four consecutive trading days... Highest yield since Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026

key_facts.fact: The 2-year yield jumped about 14.6 basis points to 4.873% and the 30-year rose to 5.434%, flattening the curve; the 10-year topped 5.10% for the first time since Jan. 22 per Yonhap Infomax.
key_facts.excerpt: The policy-sensitive 2-year yield surged 14.60bp to 4.8730%... The longest-dated 30-year Treasury yield rose 8.50bp to 5.4340%... The 10-year yield crossed the 5.10% threshold for the first time since January 22.

key_facts.fact: The sell-off was driven by higher oil after Trump's no-Iran-deal post and by expectations of further Fed rate hikes; markets had been closed Nov. 11 for Veterans Day.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury prices came under pressure as oil prices surged after President Donald Trump abruptly reversed his conciliatory stance toward Iran... Treasury market was closed the previous day for Veterans Day.

key_facts.fact: Treasuries are heading for their worst week since the April 2025 'liberation day' tariff shock, after hot October inflation and hawkish Fed remarks, as first reported by the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasuries are heading for their worst week since 'liberation day' after hot inflation and hawkish Fed comments... First reported by the Financial Times.

key_facts.fact: Context: October CPI rose 0.4% (core 0.3%), above forecasts, and traders fully price a quarter-point Fed hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting, from a current 3.75%-4% range.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders are now fully pricing in a quarter percentage-point increase when the Fed next meets Dec. 8-9... central bank officials voted 10-2 to keep their benchmark rate in a range between 3.75%-4%

key_facts.fact: Stocks ended modestly lower Nov. 12: the S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40 and the Dow 0.36% to 52,297.09.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 189.40 points, or 0.36%, to 52,297.09, the S&P 500 fell 26.98 points, or 0.35%, to 7,592.40

stories.headline: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B of North Korea's Binance haul and dismantles 'FaceStealer' deepfake scheme

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 12 the Justice Department announced court-authorized seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance, out of more than $2.7 billion frozen by government and private-sector efforts.
key_facts.excerpt: Collective U.S. government and private sector efforts so far have resulted in the freeze of more than $2.7 billion, with the Department having already obtained court-authorization to seize or restrain in excess of $1.2 billion of that amount.

key_facts.fact: The DOJ attributes the Oct. 29 theft of more than $6 billion from Binance to members of the North Korean military the FBI calls 'TraderTraitor', who are still laundering funds through bridges, mixers and exchanges.
key_facts.excerpt: on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as "TraderTraitor" stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange.

key_facts.fact: The $2.7 billion was frozen by stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle in the immediate aftermath of the break-in.
key_facts.excerpt: The department got court authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of the $2.7 billion of funds frozen by Tether and Circle Internet Group Inc. in the immediate aftermath of the Oct. 29 break-in.

key_facts.fact: Separately, the DOJ seized cloud infrastructure behind 'FaceStealer', a North Korean scheme using surreptitiously recorded videos and deepfakes that stole more than $400 million in 18 months and targeted the open-source software supply chain.
key_facts.excerpt: The scheme, which relies on surreptitiously recorded videos and artificial deepfakes, has resulted in the theft of more than $400 million in the last 18 months and the attempted compromise of individuals involved in the open-source software supply chain.

key_facts.fact: The court authorization is a step toward forfeiture, not a completed recovery; Binance has said it already covered the $6.34 billion in affected assets from its own funds.
key_facts.excerpt: The court approval is a step toward forfeiture, not a completed recovery... Binance has said it already covered the $6.34 billion in affected assets from its own funds

stories.headline: SpaceX and Tesla merger talks advance; record deal could be announced as soon as December

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Nov. 12 that SpaceX and Tesla are progressing in merger negotiations and could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as December, with early 2027 also discussed.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk's two largest companies could announce what would be the biggest-ever deal as soon as in December... The companies have also discussed a scenario in which an announcement slips into early 2027

key_facts.fact: SpaceX, public since its June IPO, is valued above $1.9 trillion and Tesla at about $1.5 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: Following its June initial public offering, SpaceX is valued at more than $1.9 trillion. Tesla is worth about $1.5 trillion.

key_facts.fact: Open issues include how to wall off Tesla's China business from SpaceX's government and defense contracts and how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive.
key_facts.excerpt: Finding a way to ring-fence Tesla's Chinese operations is among the issues under discussion... The companies are discussing how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would receive

key_facts.fact: Democrats, who take control of Congress in January after their midterm wins, have vowed to scrutinize Musk's business and political activities.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats, who will control Congress starting in January after their midterm wins, have vowed to scrutinize the business and political activities of CEO Elon Musk

key_facts.fact: Musk said in October that special committees of independent directors were formed at both boards; a deal would need backing of 50% of all Tesla shareholders. Tesla's annual meeting is Dec. 3.
key_facts.excerpt: A deal would need the backing of 50% of all Tesla shareholders, not just a majority of votes cast, he said... Tesla is scheduled to convene shareholders for its yearly meeting on Dec. 3

stories.headline: Starship Flight 15 targets Friday launch to try first catch of both booster and ship

key_facts.fact: SpaceX targets Starship Flight 15 as soon as Friday, Nov. 13, with a 75-minute window opening at 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC), pending regulatory approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Flight 15 of Starship is preparing to launch as soon as Friday, November 13, pending regulatory approval. The 75-minute launch window will open at 4:45 p.m. CT.

key_facts.fact: It is planned as the first flight to return both Super Heavy and Starship to the launch site for a tower catch; success would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system.
key_facts.excerpt: The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch. If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system

key_facts.fact: The ship is to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and fly about 14 orbits at ~275 km over more than 22 hours before attempting the catch at Starbase on Saturday; it is the first catch attempt for a V3 booster.
key_facts.excerpt: Starship's initial return-to-launch-site mission is expected to orbit the Earth at an altitude of about 275 km and complete approximately 14 orbits... over the course of a more than 22-hour flight. Starship's primary mission will be to deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites

key_facts.fact: As of Nov. 12 the FAA license, which must cover the ship's return over populated areas, was still pending.
key_facts.excerpt: Flight 15 requires a license modification, including permission for Ship 42 to return to Starbase on a trajectory which overflies populated areas... As of November 12, the launch was still pending regulatory approval.

key_facts.fact: The same weekend, Rocket Lab plans Electron's 100th launch on Nov. 14 at 5:30 UTC from New Zealand.
key_facts.excerpt: The next launch of Rocket Lab's Electron vehicle is due to lift off from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on November 14 at 5:30 UTC. This mission will serve as Electron's 100th overall mission
